//: GitHub Codespaces definition — a contributor environment that requires NOTHING
on the contributor's machine except a browser.
WHY: a collaborator without Docker, and without permission to install a Node
toolchain, cannot run the stack locally. Asking them to install one is also the
step most likely to break their machine and burn a day. A Codespace moves the
whole environment into a container GitHub runs, defined by THIS file, so:
- they install nothing and cannot 'get the setup wrong';
- everyone gets the identical Node and pnpm the CI gate uses;
- access is revoked by removing their repo permission, with nothing left
The portals need only VITE_* URLs, not a database, so a contributor can work on
the UI against a shared Directus without a local Postgres at all. Point
VITE_DIRECTUS_URL at a DEV Directus — never production: a Codespace has real
write access to whatever it is pointed at.
Ports 5173/5174 are forwarded automatically and open as private HTTPS URLs that
only the Codespace owner can reach.
